newsitem.title: USA: Layoffs rose 8.5 pct in U.S. in 1996 - Challenger.
newsitem.headline: Layoffs rose 8.5 pct in U.S. in 1996 - Challenger.

text.p: Job cuts in the United States rose 8.5 percent in 1996 to 477,147, compared with 439,882 in 1995, according to a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc.
In December, however, layoffs declined 32 percent to 37,402, compared with 55,237 in the same month of 1995.
"The slowdown in job cuts in the second half of 1996 may be a harbinger of things to come," said John Challenger, executive vice president of the outplacement firm.

Job cuts could be 10 to 15 percent lower this year than in 1996 "because today's economy is strong and a tight labor market has caused companies to rethink their former stance on the disposability of people," Challenger said.
